title: How to approach a product launch case
description: The first question to ask in a product launch case, how to structure it, and the trap to avoid.
hook: Launch cases ask how to bring something new to market. Here is a simple way to cover everything that matters.
body:
The first question to ask

Is the decision to launch made, and what must the launch achieve?

How to build your structure

  • Who to target (segment size and growth, unmet needs, competitors in the segment)
  • What to offer (product, price, channels, message)
  • How to roll it out (capabilities, pilot then scale)
  • Does it pay? (expected sales, costs, break-even, cannibalisation)

The trap most people fall into

Choosing the 4Ps before choosing the customer.

For the full tree, with every branch, read the product launch framework.

Two prompts to try

How should a snack brand launch a high-protein bar?

Show a model structure
  • Who: Target customers and their need; Size of the segment
  • What: Product, flavours, pack sizes; Price vs rivals
  • Where and how: Channels: supermarkets, gyms, online; Marketing and sampling
  • Economics and risks: Volume to break even; Cannibalisation of our other bars

Where to start: Who: a launch without a clear target customer spreads money thin.

The trap: Starting with advertising before choosing the customer and the channel.

Should a supermarket launch a premium own-label range?

Show a model structure
  • Customer demand: Shoppers buying premium brands; Willingness to trust our brand
  • Economics: Margin vs branded products; Volume needed to cover development
  • Suppliers: Who can make it at quality; Reaction of big brands
  • Cannibalisation: Sales taken from our standard own-label; Net margin gained

Where to start: Margin vs branded: premium own-label usually earns more per item.

The trap: Ignoring how the big brands might react, such as cutting promotions.
outro: Small things like this add up. Try it in your next practice case and notice how it changes the conversation. Practise this case type in the free casebook: every case has a worked answer.
